text.p: Bosnia's election was a "major victory for the democratic process" and vindicated the international community which pressed ahead with the polls over critics' objections, U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher said on Wednesday.

At a short news conference, he also said the fact that the polls were completed successfully meant the United Nations could move forward with lifting sanctions on Serbia and that NATO-led IFOR troops could be withdrawn by year's end as planned.

But Christopher acknowledged there would have to be some kind of "international presence" in the country after the IFOR (implementaiton force) is withdrawn, although the nature of that force has yet to be determined by NATO.
He also stressed the obligations of Bosnia's Moslem, Croat and Serb factions under the 1995 Dayton accords included a unified Bosnia, something many Serbs and Croats have resisted.

"This election is a major victory for the democratic process ... The large turnout demonstrated that the Bosnian people were clearly determined to go to the polls. The balloting was orderly and calm, free of violence. This is really a remarkable achievement for a country that experienced four years of war following half a century of communism," Christopher said.
"It vindicates the international community's determination to support the Bosnia people's wish to move forward with the election on a timely basis," he added.
